why: A calendar that keeps counting from a massacre is the kind of dark joke I like.
content: The Coptic year is numbered from the year Diocletian became emperor, so the count itself records a persecution.
evidence: The epoch (first day of first year) of the Coptic calendar equates to 29 August 284 AD, the year Diocletian became Roman Emperor. His reign was marked by tortures and mass executions of Christians, especially in Egypt.
